Figure 1. CARVE overview. Given a base 3D CT VLM (a Medical Text Encoder paired with a 3D vision encoder), each abnormality is scored with positive/negative prompts, yielding independent per-label probabilities. CARVE generates weak volumetric views, retains a reliable low-entropy subset (V ∗ of V views), estimates a sample-specific positive-label cardinality k̂, and updates only the visual normalization parameters via a cardinality-aware top-k̂ objective (LCARVE per view, summed into LTTA). Gradients are recomputed only for the retained views, keeping volumetric test-time adaptation memory efficient.
